principles: Operator surfaces must be useful for real scheduling but must not claim execution happened.
Project experience memory is advisory context and must remain outside Koala gate evidence.
Reuse the existing Parallel Wave model so dispatch/status/merge/report cannot drift from planning safety rules.
Every new command must be registered in CLI schema, policy, phase tools, process fact levels, and smoke tests.
No-overwrite output behavior and authority boundary must be mechanically tested.
drivers: User wants faster development through parallel story/worktree execution while preserving flow/fact anti-forgery boundaries.
Existing B-29b6 wave surfaces already compute dependencies, hotspots, hosts, evidence refs, and merge order.
Existing dev-memory storage already provides the project public experience library and must not be duplicated.

options.name: Extend Parallel Wave with read-only operator projections
pros: Smallest coherent implementation over existing safety model
Easy to test through existing lattice-parallel-wave-smoke
cons: Future runner API may need an adapter layer

options.name: Create a separate dispatch subsystem with its own model
pros: Clean namespace for future execution API
cons: Higher drift risk between planning and dispatch
More files and policy registrations for similar facts

options.name: Add real automatic agent spawning now
cons: No signed host-runner dispatch API in this CLI yet
Harder to verify without external actor receipts

chosen: Extend Parallel Wave with read-only operator projections
rationale: This preserves the existing safety and authority model while giving operators actionable dispatch, status, merge, and report outputs now. It also keeps dev-memory as bounded context instead of a competing truth source.

preMortem.scenario: The dispatch manifest is mistaken for proof that an agent actually executed work.
preMortem.trigger: Output says dispatched or uses actor-success wording.
preMortem.consequence: Flow forgery risk returns through a planning artifact.
preMortem.mitigation: Use spawned:false, requiresRunnerConfirmation:true, authority.productionDone:false, and test these fields.

preMortem.scenario: Dev-memory entries are treated as gate evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Report includes experienceRefs without non-authoritative markers.
preMortem.consequence: Fact quality drops because lessons replace evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Experience refs carry gateEvidence:false and authority:non_authoritative, and smoke asserts they do not alter receiptRefs.

preMortem.scenario: New commands appear in CLI help but not policy/fact registries.
preMortem.trigger: MAIN_TOOLS updated without COMMAND_POLICIES or PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS.
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke asserts MAIN_TOOLS, registry, command-policy, default phase tools, and process fact registrations for all new commands.

preMortem.scenario: Merge queue guidance encourages unsafe merge order.
preMortem.trigger: Dependency blockers and plan-only hotspots are hidden in ready entries.
preMortem.consequence: Parallel speedup causes integration conflicts or unreviewed sequencing.
preMortem.mitigation: Merge queue entries expose readyForMerge, blockers, after dependencies, and recommendations from existing wave safety.
